title: “BFRB Buddy” for the Assessment of Body-Focused Repetitive Behaviors
summary:
Body-focused repetitive behaviors (BFRBs), such as nail biting, skin picking, or compulsive hair pulling, affect many people and can be associated with considerable physical and psychological distress. The aim of this study is to investigate a digital self-monitoring system (“BFRB Buddy”) designed to support individuals with BFRBs in becoming aware of their behaviors at an earlier stage during computer use.
The program uses the computer’s built-in camera or webcam to detect the position of the hands relative to the face in real time. If typical target areas, such as the mouth, hair, or face, are touched for a predefined period of time, the program immediately provides brief feedback in the form of an audio signal or temporary screen dimming. Camera images are processed exclusively locally and are neither stored nor transmitted.
A total of 128 individuals with body-focused repetitive behaviors are to be randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a waitlist control group. The intervention group will use “BFRB Buddy” for six weeks. Online questionnaires will be completed before and after the study period. The aim of the study is to investigate whether the habit-tracking system improves awareness of one’s own harmful body-focused repetitive behaviors.

interventions.name: Intervention group: Use of the computer-based habit-tracking system “BFRB Buddy” for six weeks during regular computer use. Waitlist control group: No use of “BFRB Buddy” during the six-week study period. Following completion of the T1 assessment at 6 weeks, participants in the waitlist control group will also receive access to the system.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Regular computer use, access to a functioning webcam or integrated computer camera, sufficient German language proficiency, provision of written informed consent, willingness to participate in two online interviews (T0, T1) and complete online questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient technical requirements, unwillingness to use the computer’s webcam or integrated camera, lack of informed consent, acute suicidality, diagnosis of an addictive disorder
